claims.text: Short-range chemical order creates spatial fluctuations in local shear-fault energy.
Persistent local shear-fault-energy fluctuations provide a strength contribution unique to concentrated alloys.
Local shear-fault-energy fluctuations resist dislocation motion.
Resistance from local fault-energy fluctuations can dominate strengthening from elastic misfit in concentrated alloys.
Rapid quenching produces a random NiCoCr solid solution with minimal short-range order.
Controlled annealing enhances short-range chemical order in NiCoCr.
Increasing short-range order increases the magnitude of local shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
Annealing-induced increases in local fault-energy fluctuations increase the yield strength of NiCoCr.
Larger local fault-energy fluctuations produce more dislocation-pinning events.
Enhanced short-range order promotes nonuniform or wavy dislocation paths.
Short-range-order-induced fault-energy fluctuations can alter twinning behavior.
CrCoNi, which is the same elemental alloy system as NiCoCr, has a metastable or thermodynamically unstable FCC lattice at ambient conditions.
The proposed mechanism remains operative at moderately elevated temperatures while the FCC phase remains metastable.
Chemical complexity in FCC concentrated alloys induces significant local fault-energy variations.
The mechanism may not apply to BCC or HCP alloys because other deformation mechanisms dominate there.
Atom-probe tomography or high-resolution TEM can quantify the degree of short-range order in the proposed specimens.
Atomistic simulation or high-resolution imaging can map local shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
A matched comparison between rapidly quenched and annealed NiCoCr specimens can isolate the effect of enhanced short-range order.
Failure of the annealed specimens to show both increased local fault-energy fluctuations and corresponding mechanical or dislocation changes would falsify the hypothesis.
